answerCheck.reason: The line-plane incidence axiom makes every point of the line a point of the plane once two distinct points are shared. A single shared point would not suffice: the z-axis and plane z=0 share only the origin. The ordinary school phrase two points is understood as distinct here; the proposed node makes that condition explicit.
Two distinct points on the line and the external point are noncollinear, so they determine a unique plane containing the line and point.
In the line-plane position classification, intersecting means having exactly one common point, unlike a line contained in the plane.

A plane through cube vertices that avoids the interior is supporting; containing three vertices forces its intersection with the cube to be a face. There are C(8,3) = 56 triples and 6C(4,3) = 24 face triples, with no duplication. The probability is (56-24)/56 = 4/7.

flags: Inside is interpreted as the strict three-dimensional interior, rather than including the cube's boundary.
